summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares azenosertib with chemotherapy chosen by the investigator in women with platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer whose tumors are positive for cyclin E1 protein. Azenosertib 400 mg is taken by mouth, and the chemotherapy (paclitaxel, gemcitabine, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or topotecan, chosen by the investigator) is given intravenously; the duration and schedule are not stated. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is randomized, open-label, and Phase 3.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara azenosertib con quimioterapia elegida por el investigador en mujeres con cáncer de ovario seroso de alto grado resistente al platino, cáncer peritoneal primario o cáncer de trompa de Falopio cuyos tumores son positivos para la proteína ciclina E1. El azenosertib de 400 mg se toma por vía oral, y la quimioterapia (paclitaxel, gemcitabina, doxorrubicina liposomal pegilada o topotecán, elegida por el investigador) se administra por vía intravenosa; la duración y el esquema no se indican. El desenlace principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es aleatorizado, abierto y de fase 3.
who_for: Women 18 or older with high-grade serous ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer.
Platinum-resistant disease with 1 to 3 prior treatment lines (up to 4 if prior mirvetuximab).
Tumor positive for cyclin E1 protein by the sponsor's test.
Measurable disease and ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
Prior bevacizumab, PARP inhibitor (if BRCA or HRD), or mirvetuximab required when standard of care allows.
not_for: Prior WEE1, ATR, CHK1/2, or PKMYT1 inhibitor for ovarian cancer.
Another cancer within the previous 2 years, with listed exceptions.
Recent chemotherapy, targeted therapy, radiation, major surgery, or investigational drug within set time frames.
Serious conditions such as unstable brain metastases, bowel obstruction, or active hepatitis B or C.
